sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Merano's policy is a mix of paid street parking and cameras at the edge of the old centre. The city's Blue Park ordinance of 13 February 2023 divides paid street parking into Zone A, paid every day, and Zone B, paid Monday to Saturday, with residents without a private space, social institutions and people with disabilities able to apply for subscriptions [1]. The city's own page, last updated on 7 May 2026, says blue spaces are paid Monday to Sunday from 08:00 to 19:00 and that only the actual parking time is paid by app, which simplifies the ordinance [2]. In December 2022 the municipal executive decided on tariffs of 2.50 euros an hour in Zone A and 1.50 euros in Zone B from the start of 2023, with annual subscriptions of 280 euros for the first and 420 euros for the second; the page does not say whether these are still current [0]. Restricted traffic zones are monitored by cameras at four points: Postbrucke, Obere Freiheitsstrasse/Theaterplatz, Galileistrasse and Zenobergstrasse, with fines issued automatically [3]. The city council approved the mobility plan (PUMS) and the traffic plan (PGTU) on 11 March 2025 [4].

The next change is tied to a tunnel. On 7 October 2026 the city presented a mobility concept, 'Kurstadt 2.0', and plans first city-centre measures from January 2027: traffic calming, reversed flows in some streets and a reorganisation of central-area parking linked to the new Kavernengarage. The north-west bypass is scheduled to open on 21 November 2026 and carry traffic from 26 November; a shuttle bus to the hospital, Rennweg, the baths and Untermais station is only an idea so far [5].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The Kavernengarage under the Küchelberg is the large project. It is a public-private partnership: private partners financed it fully in return for a 50-year concession, and it is planned with 594 spaces, 12 EV charging stations and car-sharing spaces, with a cost that rose from 27 to 39 million euros and an opening not before 2026 because access depends on the second bypass tunnel section [7]. In February 2025 it was reported to be due to open together with the Küchelberg tunnel, planned for autumn 2026, and the municipality had spent about 6 million euros on securing works against an estimate of 3.7 million two years earlier [9]. The city's October 2026 release gives no opening date or price for the garage [5]. Terms reported in 2019 included a maximum hourly rate of 2.40 euros and a monthly pass capped at 183 euros, but the final contract was not checked [8].

The hospital is the other pressure point: the city says its car park is full on weekdays in school term from roughly 07:30 to 12:00, and a plan for the health area envisages about 700 spaces, 155 more than today [6]. On 30 December 2024 the province gave the start signal for a mobility centre at the railway station, with about 350 underground parking spaces mainly for commuters and a cost of about 28.4 million euros, planning to start in 2025 and building in 2026 [14]. Neogy was commissioned in 2023 to install 18 new charging columns at 11 locations, aiming at 50 public charge points by 2025 [13].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Stadtwerke Meran, wholly owned by the municipality, lists parking lots and garages among its responsibilities, but its page names no locations or rates [15]. The Therme Meran garage is run by the baths: day-ticket holders can add 16 euros to park until midnight, and with a 2 to 3 hour ticket the first hour is free and each further hour costs 3.20 euros [11]. The St. Josef garage advertises 90 public spaces and 1.40 euros per half hour [12]. According to a written question by three South Tyrol Landtag members in August 2026, 347,598 vehicles used the Therme garage in the previous year, bringing in more than 2.3 million euros; they say that revenue is likely to fall once the tunnel and Kavernengarage open if motorised traffic is really kept out of the centre. No reply was found [10].

Our data cover six car parks with 1,510 spaces from the South Tyrol open-data platform, measured since late September 2026. Occupancy averaged about 37% on weekdays and 34% at weekends, weighted by spaces, so Merano's garages hardly change between weekday and weekend. The Algunder Kellerei garage (255 spaces) is the fullest at 63% on average and reached 94% on a Friday at noon. The St. Josef lot (132 spaces in our feed against the 90 public ones it advertises) averaged 37%, reached 99% on a Tuesday and was full for about 9% of the hours. Park Karl Wolf averaged 42% and peaked at 92%. The Therme garage, the largest at 545 spaces, averaged 30%, and the Plaza shopping-centre garage (321) 23%. So even the busiest garages have room outside the midday peak. This is about three weeks of data, taken in autumn and not at the Christmas market.
